- Controller/processor: their redline flips a couple of clauses to make Redwood a joint controller for telemetry. We should push back and keep telemetry as a processor activity with described purposes.
- SCCs: they asked about the "addendum" (EEA->US). We can accept the 2021 SCCs and sign the supplementary transfer impact appendix, but we need ops to confirm actual hosting footprint and whether on-prem/Private deployment is required for EU-resident PH customers.

I uploaded an annotated Order Form: Redline_MSA_OrderForm_PulseHealth_annotated.docx and left comments next to the liability and telemetry sections. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-pulse-dpa-review

- High level: accept most DPA language except the three carveouts (liability, joint-control telemetry language, and an ambig. subprocessor obligation).
- Attach: our proposed DPA redline and a 1-page transfer appendix (ops).
- Offer: a 30-minute legal + security sync with PulseHealth this week if they'd like to walk the changes.

1) Controller/Processor: PulseHealth wants to keep some decisioning rights described in our operations clauses that could imply joint controllership. Proposed language: insert a short definition in the DPA that lists telemetry, usage metrics, and support diagnostics as processor activities for Redwood with examples of purposes. 3) Subprocessor notification: accept their request for 30-day notice but keep a standard "opportunity to object" process tied to a documented risk assessment; do not accept unilateral veto rights.
